decks.notes: The deck focuses on using artifact ramp cards like Mana Crypt and Moxen to power out powerful threats like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge. It also utilizes cards like Sensei's Divining Top and Manifold Key to manipulate the top of the deck and generate card advantage. The deck aims to play aggressive creatures like Nettlecyst and Glaring Fleshraker to quickly overwhelm the opponent while utilizing cards like Time Vault and The One Ring to generate extra turns and close out the game. The deck is focused on a fast-paced aggressive strategy using artifact synergy as its main engine.

The deck aims to utilize Paradoxical Outcome to draw a large number of cards and generate mana for a powerful combo win condition. By cycling through cards with various artifacts and spells like Mana Vault, Moxen, and Lórien Revealed, the deck can set up a strong board state quickly. It also includes disruption and protection spells like Force of Will and Force of Negation to control the game. With key pieces like Time Vault and Time Walk, the strategy is to create a dominant position and win the game in a short amount of time.

This deck focuses on utilizing powerful, disruptive creatures and spells to control the board while pressuring the opponent. It includes a mix of efficient removal in cards like Fatal Push and Abrupt Decay, along with strong threats like Oko, Thief of Crowns and Leovold, Emissary of Trest. The deck also has access to strong card advantage and selection with cards like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. By disrupting the opponent's game plan and applying pressure, this deck aims to win the game quickly and decisively.

The main concept of this deck is to utilize graveyard mechanics and self-mill to quickly fill the graveyard with creatures and then bring them back onto the battlefield for a powerful combo finish. By utilizing cards like Golgari Thug, Stinkweed Imp, and Bazaar of Baghdad, the deck can efficiently dredge cards into the graveyard. Cards like Narcomoeba, Ichorid, and Prized Amalgam can then be brought back onto the battlefield for a powerful offensive strategy. Additionally, the deck includes disruption cards like Force of Will and Mindbreak Trap to protect the combo.

The main focus of the deck is to control the game through counterspells, removal, and card advantage, while utilizing Lurrus as a companion for extra value. The deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan and maintain control of the game through efficient use of resources such as the Moxen and powerful spells like Ancestral Recall and Demonic Tutor. The inclusion of various cantrips and card draw spells help to assemble the necessary pieces for victory, while strong creatures like Snapcaster Mage provide additional threats and utility.

This deck focuses on establishing early board control and disrupting the opponent's strategy with mana denial effects and artifacts like Trinisphere and Null Rod. Golos, Tireless Pilgrim serves as a versatile threat and card advantage engine, while Mishra's Workshop enables explosive starts. The deck utilizes powerful artifacts such as Nettlecyst and Crucible of Worlds to outvalue the opponent, with cards like Stonecoil Serpent providing additional threats. By combining aggro elements with artifact synergies, this deck aims to overwhelm the opponent and secure victories through resource denial and efficient threats.

The main focus of this deck is to establish a strong board presence quickly using artifact creatures and mana acceleration. By utilizing cards like Mishra's Workshop, Ancient Tomb, and Grim Monolith, the deck is able to quickly ramp into threats like Glaring Fleshraker and Lodestone Golem. Manifold Key and The One Ring provide additional utility by granting evasion or pumping up creatures. Mystic Forge and Sensei's Divining Top help to control the top of the library, while Karn, the Great Creator can shut down opposing artifacts. The goal is to overwhelm the opponent with a fast, aggressive plan backed up by powerful artifacts.

This deck focuses on efficiently generating mana and card advantage to assemble a powerful combo utilizing cards like Paradoxical Outcome and Urza's Saga. The goal is to generate a large amount of mana, draw a significant number of cards, and ultimately win the game through a synergistic combination of spells and permanents. The deck also utilizes counterspells and removal to protect the combo pieces and disrupt the opponent's game plan. Overall, the key concept of this deck is to leverage card advantage and mana acceleration to execute a game-winning combo efficiently.

This Dimir Control deck utilizes efficient removal spells, countermagic, and card advantage to disrupt and control the opponent's game plan. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for recurring small threats and card advantage. The deck also runs a mix of powerful Vintage restricted cards like Ancestral Recall and Time Walk alongside disruptive cards like Wasteland and Force of Will. The goal is to establish and maintain control of the game through card advantage and efficient removal until the opponent is unable to recover.

This deck revolves around using Oath of Druids to quickly bring out powerful creatures like Atraxa, Grand Unifier and Lórien Revealed. It also focuses on control elements with cards like Force of Will and Counterspells to protect your creatures and disrupt your opponent's game plan. The deck includes cards like Show and Tell to cheat out big threats and powerful spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time to maintain card advantage. Additionally, the deck utilizes versatile lands like Boseiju, Who Endures to ensure key spells resolve successfully.

The deck focuses on using Paradoxical Outcome to generate mana and draw cards while controlling the opponent with counterspells and removal. The key strategy is to create a loop of playing artifacts, bouncing them back to hand with Paradoxical Outcome, and replaying them to generate more mana and dig deeper into the deck for win conditions like Thundertrap Trainer. The inclusion of powerful Vintage staples like Time Walk, Ancestral Recall, and Black Lotus allows for explosive plays and versatile options to outmaneuver the opponent.

The deck focuses on playing disruptive creatures while also using hate cards to slow down opponents. It aims to control the game by limiting the opponent's options and board presence. By using a combination of hatebears and aggressive creatures, the deck can apply pressure while also stopping the opponent from executing their game plan effectively. The addition of powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen allows for explosive starts and provides additional resources to keep the pressure on. Overall, the strategy combines aggression with disruption to gain a significant advantage in the early game.

This deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy by playing hatebears, such as Archon of Emeria and Thalia, Guardian of Thraben, while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper and White Plume Adventurer. The deck also utilizes disruptive artifacts like Chalice of the Void and Trinisphere to further hinder the opponent's plans. The goal is to establish a board presence quickly and disrupt the opponent's game plan, allowing the deck to control the pace of the game and secure a victory.

This deck focuses on generating mana and card advantage through artifacts like Moxen, Black Lotus, and Mishra's Bauble. It uses cards like Paradoxical Outcome and Lórien Revealed to bounce and replay these artifacts, generating more mana and drawing cards. The deck also has disruptive elements like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares to protect the combo. The goal is to amass a large amount of mana and draw through the deck quickly to find win conditions like Thundertrap Trainer or Flame of Anor to close out the game.

This deck focuses on using Paradoxical Outcome to generate card advantage and mana to set up powerful combos. It utilizes a variety of fast mana sources like Moxen and Mana Crypt to accelerate into its combo pieces quickly. The deck also includes disruption in the form of counterspells like Force of Will and Force of Negation, as well as removal spells like Swords to Plowshares. The goal is to quickly assemble a winning combination of cards and overwhelm the opponent before they can respond effectively.

The deck focuses on utilizing the graveyard as a resource to quickly overwhelm the opponent with a combination of powerful creatures and disruptive spells. By discarding cards like Narcomoeba and Creeping Chill, the deck can trigger abilities that allow for explosive plays, while also using cards like Force of Will and Force of Negation to protect its game plan. Additionally, the deck includes cards like Ichorid and Prized Amalgam to create a constant stream of threats, ensuring that the opponent is always under pressure.
